notes: M3.3 deliverable: scaffold + 5 invariants (INV-01, INV-07, INV-09, INV-11, INV-13).
Encoding `query` fields are paths relative to this manifest.json (i.e. relative to aegisgraph/invariants/).
`expected_violations: "unknown"` is the honest baseline for real SMA targets we have not yet ground-truthed; demo-vulnerable-app fixtures land in M3.4.
Full 25-30 invariants ship across M3-M11 per Phase II rollout plan; manifest entries are additive and the schema permits future fields.

invariants.statement: Attacker-controlled URL strings shall not reach outbound network calls (OkHttp newCall, HttpURLConnection, Ktor, Retrofit) without passing through an allowlist or policy checker.
invariants.rationale: Unchecked URL fetches enable SSRF, internal-network probing, private-IP exfiltration, and exploitation of redirect-following parsers. The CodeQL taint analysis detects URL strings from message bodies, deep-link URIs, push payloads, and QR-encoded URLs flowing to HTTP-client invocations without traversing a recognized policy barrier.

invariants.statement: AndroidManifest <intent-filter> elements declared on an exported component shall not omit a guarding android:permission (or signature-level permission) when the component handles attacker-reachable actions or data schemes.
invariants.rationale: An exported activity, service, or receiver with an open intent-filter and no permission gate is reachable from any installed app. Combined with weak input validation in the handler, this is a textbook lateral-movement path. The Semgrep rule detects AndroidManifest XML patterns where android:exported="true" (or implicit-exported via intent-filter on pre-Android-12 components) appears without a matching android:permission attribute.

invariants.statement: Android WebView instances shall not call addJavascriptInterface() on user-controlled content without setting setAllowFileAccess(false), setAllowContentAccess(false), and a same-origin guard on the bound object.
invariants.rationale: addJavascriptInterface bridges the JS execution context into the host app, exposing reflectively-callable Java methods. When the WebView loads attacker-influenced HTML (link preview, federated room content, oEmbed) without origin restrictions, the bridge becomes a remote code execution surface. The Semgrep rule (stub at M3.3, fully encoded at M5.3) detects addJavascriptInterface call sites without preceding hardening calls.

invariants.statement: Deep-link handlers shall not invoke startActivity / Custom Tabs / WebView.loadUrl with a URL parsed from an inbound intent (Intent.getData, intent.getDataString) unless the URL passed through a host/scheme allowlist.
invariants.rationale: Open-redirect-style abuse of deep links lets an attacker get the messenger app to load a URL of their choosing — useful for phishing, OAuth-flow hijacking, and as a SSRF amplifier when combined with INV-01. The CodeQL query (stub at M3.3, fully encoded at M3.4) tracks intent.getData/getDataString through host activities to the first outbound load without an intervening allowlist check.

invariants.statement: QR-code-initiated device linking flows shall bind the QR payload to a verified key-exchange round-trip (X3DH, Noise, MLS keypair confirmation) before any session key, identity claim, or sync token is provisioned.
invariants.rationale: Provisioning a session from an unverified QR payload allows a tampered QR (printed, shoulder-surfed, MITM-relayed) to silently link an attacker device into a victim's account. The CodeQL query (stub at M3.3, fully encoded at M3.4) detects QR-payload data sources (camera intent results, image-decoded QR strings) reaching a device-link provisioning sink (session keystore, identity key registration, sync-state initializer) without a KEX-completion barrier.
